implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__ creates a grid with default rows=6, columns=7 and stores rows/columns attributes.
Game stores players in a list and switches turns with Game.switch_player; Game.play loops calling current_player.get_move each iteration.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: Player.get_move prompts with input() and parses a 1‑based column number.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range, numeric, not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Player.get_move checks .isdigit(), board.is_valid_column, and board.has_empty_slot, re‑prompting on failure.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop disc into the lowest empty slot of the chosen column
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.drop_disc iterates from bottom row upward, places the disc, and returns the row index.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Render the board after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.render prints the grid; Game.play calls board.render before the loop and after each successful drop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a win (four in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win examines four directions from the last placed disc and returns True when count >= 4.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect a draw when the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full checks that every top cell is occupied; Game.play ends with a draw message when it returns True.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graceful termination on win, draw, or user interrupt
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play returns after win or draw; main() catches KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError and prints a goodbye message.

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, interactive Connect Four game matching the benchmark description. Core mechanics—grid creation, turn‑based input, validation, disc placement, board rendering, win/draw detection, and graceful exit—are all present and appear syntactically correct, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
